title: Introduce lightweight premerge pipeline and dependency auditor
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: our current premerge CI is heavy for small syntactic / manifest-only changes and gives noisy dependency signals that slow developer feedback. This PR introduces a lightweight premerge pipeline (fastpath) plus a dependency auditor that surfaces risky transitive upgrades during PR authoring. The aim is to speed fast feedback for iterative work while providing an automated hygiene check for dependency drift. Scope: (1) a new fastpath workflow that runs lint subsets, unit smoke, and a minimal dependency-extract step; (2) a dependency-auditor action that scores transitive changes, highlights license/security red flags, and produces an artifacts/summary JSON for engineers; (3) integration with our Slack premerge-bot to post the auditor score and suggested remediation links; (4) a small refactor of existing lint workflow to make it callable as a composite action. Implementation notes: the fastpath workflow uses path filters and a two-stage matrix to avoid expensive setup where not needed; the auditor runs a containerized analyzer based on OSV + internal heuristics and returns a numerical score (0-100) and a short human-readable summary. The PR implements a conservative default: only paths that touch src/, packages/, or build-config/ trigger the full pipeline; docs/ or markdown-only changes take the fastpath. Checklist: - [x] fastpath workflow and composite lint action - [x] dependency-auditor action and container image + Dockerfile - [x] Slack integration and small message template - [x] tests for auditor heuristics (unit + small e2e) - [x] docs in dev-infra/ci/README - [x] migration note for contributors Rollout plan: fastpath is enabled for all PRs on main but defaults to run in 'fast' lane; auditor is opt-out per-repo initially (set via repo-level config). We'll monitor false negatives for a week, then flip auditor to required for backend and SDK repos if stable. Follow-ups: extend auditor to annotate PR file comments and wire a remediation guide for typical transitive flags. Related: ENG-3245 (CI feedback speed), ENG-3278 (dep hygiene), SUP-881 (customer incident caused by transitive license regression).

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative on enforcement. Auditor scoring is advisory during the initial rollout. Team will iterate thresholds based on signals from the next two weeks of PR traffic.
